_: SecurityInsight Pro -- THE CONFIGURATION SET (#404, framework CONFIG-1). Every customer-made configuration record in the Pro database: what the change journal (cfg.ConfigJournal, one trigger per table) records, what the configuration backup (cfg.vConfigSnapshot) copies, and what undo / restore may write back. ONE list, read by the schema generator (engine\pro-settings\Build-SIConfigJournalSql.ps1 -> the GENERATED CONFIG JOURNAL block of sql\si-pro-settings.sql), by PowerShell (SI-ConfigJournal.ps1) and by the web app (Config\ConfigEntities.cs, linked next to the app). EVERY cfg table is either an entity or listed under notConfiguration with its reason -- a test fails on a table that is neither, and on a column that is in neither 'columns' nor 'ignore'. Fields: table; pk (the stored row's primary key, how the trigger pairs before and after); identity (an IDENTITY column, never written back); key (the record's key across commits and backups -- a natural key where a re-add writes a new row); columns (the record, in this order); meta (stamps: kept in the record, ignored when comparing and never restored); ignore (never recorded: rowversions and run-time counters); soft (a soft removal: at / by -- a record is in force while 'at' is NULL; a remove sets it, never deletes); backup (in the configuration backup); undo (undo and restore may write it back -- otherwise the reason says why not); source (a fixed journal source for every write); minRole (the role that may change it, also when undoing / restoring); changeLogScope (the cfg.ChangeLog scope an undo / restore writes).

entities.label: Template overrides (risk index, report, rule, tagging, CMDB and service model edits)
Guard acknowledgements
entities.noUndoWhy: an acknowledgement records that a person read a guard event -- it is kept as a record and belongs to that event, so it is never undone or restored

entities.label: Templates installed by the product
entities.noUndoWhy: templates are installed by the product with each release (template split): they are journaled, never backed up, and rolled back on the Template releases page -- your own edits are template overrides, which are backed up
